key_insight: Longitudinal ribs trigger counter-rotating secondary vortices and strongly alter near-wall turbulence, with rectangular ribs producing a larger roughness effect than triangular ribs.
engineering_relevance: Rib shape and spacing can be tuned to control wall shear, turbulence production, and mixing/drag behavior in internal flows such as channels and ducts.
method: Large Eddy Simulation (LES) of channel flow at friction Reynolds number Reτ = 220
Compared two surface-mounted longitudinal rib geometries: rectangular and triangular
Used rib aspect ratio W/h = 2 and spacing S = 0.6H to assess secondary flow and near-wall statistics
evidence_signal: The abstract reports two counter-rotating vortices in both cases, higher roughness function for rectangular ribs, and near-wall stress/production differences supported by Reynolds stress and TKE profiles.
watch_item: Results are from a single Reynolds number and a specific rib spacing/aspect ratio, so the trends may not generalize without further parametric testing.
paper_title: Secondary Flows and Near-Wall Turbulence in Channel Flow with Longitudinal Ribs
